import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Create a summary DataFrame for total sales per product
sales_summary = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Create a barplot for total sales per product
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='total', y='product', data=sales_summary, palette='viridis')
plt.title('Total Sales by Product')
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Product')
plt.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the plot as a PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Create a summary DataFrame for total sales per product
sales_summary = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Create a barplot for total sales per product
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='total', y='product', data=sales_summary, palette='viridis')
plt.title('Total Sales by Product')
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Product')
plt.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the plot as a PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
